elements.quote: Much of the evidence remains very low certainty, and we anticipate that future studies evaluating drugs for prophylaxis may substantially change the results, particularly for outcomes of laboratory confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and mortality.
elements.reason: The text describes the current state of knowledge (very low certainty evidence) and the important uncertainties regarding the results for prophylaxis drugs.

elements.quote: Effective prophylaxis for covid-19 could have a global impact in preventing infection and attenuating disease
elements.reason: The text explains the importance of the review by highlighting the potential global impact of effective prophylaxis for COVID-19.

elements.quote: This is the second iteration of our living network meta-analysis on prophylaxis for covid-19
elements.reason: The review explicitly identifies itself as an update (second iteration) of a previous version of the same living systematic review.
The review evaluates multiple different prophylactic drugs (e.g., hydroxychloroquine, vitamin C, ivermectin, etc.) rather than a single intervention with a specific mechanism of action to describe.
The review does not utilize a logic model to describe complex intervention components or delivery contexts.

While the document mentions that patients participated in defining clinical questions (chunk_20) and that the protocol provides detailed methods (chunk_10), the manuscript does not explicitly state the specific research objective or question(s) the review addresses in a clear, formal manner.

elements.quote: Randomisedtrials in which people at risk of covid-19 were allocated to prophylaxis or no prophylaxis (standard care or placebo).
elements.reason: The review defines the planned comparison (prophylaxis vs. no prophylaxis/standard care/placebo) for the intervention effects, which constitutes a PICO-like structure.

elements.quote: Weincluded randomised trials of people at risk of covid-19 that compared drugs, therapeutic doses of vitamins, or antibodies for prophylaxis against one another or against no prophylaxis (placebo or standard care, as defined by the researchers), with no restriction onlanguageofpublication. We included studies addressing people pre- or post-exposure to covid-19 and at low risk (e.g. unexposed community member) or high risk (e.g. member of the same household with one or more positive cases, contact of index case, healthcare worker or long term care resident) for covid-19.
elements.reason: The text specifies the study design (randomised trials), population (people at risk of covid-19, pre- or post-exposure, low or high risk), and intervention (drugs, therapeutic doses of vitamins, or antibodies for prophylaxis).

elements.quote: with no restriction onlanguageofpublication.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly states there is no restriction on the language of publication. The review does not report excluding studies specifically because outcomes were not measured versus not reported; therefore, this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.reason: The manuscript specifies that studies were grouped by intervention type (drugs, antibody, and cellular therapies) for separate network meta-analyses.
There are no notable restrictions on study eligibility that require a specific rationale beyond standard systematic review inclusion criteria.
